title: SDK/API launch: content stencils, compatibility matrix, telemetry contract and sample prompt kits
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Goal: produce a set of canonical content artifacts for the SDK/API v2 launch that engineering, design, and growth teams can reuse: (1) lightweight content stencils for each surface (text generation, function calling, structured output, streaming), (2) an SDK⇄API compatibility matrix that maps feature flags and breaking changes across SDK versions and runtime releases, (3) a telemetry event contract with required fields and sample payloads, and (4) a curated set of sample prompt kits (including prompt templates and test harnesses) for customers and samples pages.

Problem context and constraints: the new function-calling and structured-output options introduce shape changes in responses that must be reflected in sample code across Node/Python/Go SDKs and in the hosted docs. Streaming samples require different examples (partial/patch events) and the telemetry contract must capture streaming lifecycle events (open/patch/close) for accurate cost/latency dashboards. We must avoid divergent copies of samples across repos and ensure PRs are easy to review by non-engineers.

Decisions so far: use canonical markdown stencils stored in a single content repo (https://github.com/redwood-inference/content-stencils) and reference them from each SDK repo via submodule or CI fetch. The compatibility matrix will be a single CSV in the content repo and a machine-readable JSON that the docs site uses in the release notes page. Telemetry contract will be versioned (telemetry.v1) and require fields: request_id, model, sdk_version, endpoint_variant, batching_info (nullable string), stream_event (nullable enum), kv_cache_hit_rate (nullable number). Sample prompt kits will include three scenarios per feature (basic, best-practices, and anti-pattern) and each kit will include unit tests used by the docs regen job.

Trade-offs discussed: strict centralization reduces drift but adds friction for fast fix PRs in SDK repos; to balance we allow small local overrides for language-specific idioms with a mandatory link back to the canonical stencil. We considered embedding telemetry schemas directly into the runtime repo but decided on content repo hosting to keep docs and launch artifacts in one place.

Open risks: engineering ETA for streaming event hooks (ENG-21458) is still a dependency; if delayed, we will ship docs with simulated streaming events and clearly flag live telemetry as "coming soon". There is a localization workload unknown; current launch will default to en-US with a localization follow-up.

Primary deliverables: canonical markdown stencils, compatibility CSV+JSON, telemetry schema JSON examples, sample prompt kits (Node/Python/Go) with tests, docsite PR templates, release-notes blurb templates.
acceptance_criteria: All content artifacts committed to content-stencils repo under /releases/sdk-2.0 by due_date
Compatibility matrix CSV and machine JSON consumed by docs site and displayed on release notes page
Telemetry contract published as telemetry.v1 JSON with sample payloads and a short explainer on Confluence
Sample prompt kits for function calling, structured output, and streaming present in /kits with runnable unit tests
Pull request templates created and used by all three SDK repos; docs PR checklist includes compatibility matrix and telemetry link
